title: A Unified Design Flow for Homogeneous and Heterogeneous 3D Integration with Fine-Pitch Hybrid Bonding
problem: Existing EDA tools lack native support for multi-tier 3D IC integration with fine-pitch hybrid bonding, leading to 3D via overflow and design rule violations when using pseudo-3D flows based on conventional 2D tools.
motivation: Enable efficient 3D IC design with native support for 3D-specific constraints like via count limitations and pitch overlaps, particularly for heterogeneous integration across different technology nodes.
method: Unified 3D IC design framework with four key techniques: (1) Generalized footprint contraction for heterogeneous/homogeneous integration; (2) Constraint-driven tier partitioning for pitch-based 3D via budgeting; (3) Timing-aware gain steering performance-critical cells to faster die; (4) Post-route 3D via legalization using reinforcement learning.
key_novelty: First unified 3D IC design framework supporting both homogeneous and heterogeneous 3D integrations with native constraint handling.
contributions: Reduces 3D via count by up to 62% with 45-89% via utilization
Improves WNS by up to 62% and TNS by up to 74% through timing-aware cell assignment
Eliminates overlapping 3D vias using RL-based post-route legalization
Supports heterogeneous 3D ICs with different technology nodes

metrics.ppa: 62% WNS improvement, 74% TNS improvement, 62% via reduction

baselines: Conventional pseudo-3D flows based on 2D tools
limitations: Evaluated on homogeneous and heterogeneous 3D benchmarks; specific to fine-pitch hybrid bonding integration.
primary_theme: Unified 3D IC design with constraint-driven optimization
